newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing confident as replies to EU deal query.
newsitem.headline: Boeing confident as replies to EU deal query.

text.p: Boeing Co. expressed hope on Tuesday about European Commission approval of its merger with rival aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas after meeting an overnight EU deadline for replying to queries on the deal's effects.
"We submitted a document last night which summarised our discussions of last week," Boeing's vice president for European affairs Jim Frank told Reuters.
He said he was optimistic about regulators' reaction to the submission, supplied to meet the Commission's deadline of midnight local time (2200 GMT).
"We submitted constructive proposals in each of the areas which had been identified," he said.

Frank said three areas of Commission concern were Boeing's exclusive supply deals with three U.S. airlines, the size of its $14 billion merger with McDonnell Douglas and the danger of spillovers between the merged companies' defence and civil aviation activities.
He gave no details about the submission.
The European Commission is set to present its thinking on the Boeing case to an advisory committee of EU national competition officials next Friday.
Frank said Boeing had kept national officials in the frame.

"We have been in touch with them to brief them about what we have been up to," he said, adding that their reactions had "spanned the spectrum of what you would expect, from those protective of Airbus to the others".

Boeing's merger with its former U.S. rival leaves the European Airbus consortium, whose parent companies hail from Germany, France, Britain and Spain, as the only other supplier of medium-sized and larger commercial aircraft.
